A man ran into my clinic holding the left side of his chest, shouting, Doctor, my heart is failing!
Stay till the end, because what I told him could save a life one day.
I asked him, why are you pressing there? He said, because that's where the heart is, Doctor. Everyone knows that.
So I showed him. Your heart actually sits almost in the middle of your chest, right behind the breastbone. Only about two thirds of it leans left.
But then why do we feel the beat on the left? Because the tip of the heart, the apex, taps the chest wall right there.
Wait, it gets stranger. About one in twelve thousand people are born with their heart pointing to the right.
His ECG was normal. It was acidity this time. But chest pain should always be checked, never guessed.
And if someone collapses, push hard in the centre of the chest, not the left. That's CPR.
